title: Health & pharmacy
body:
Police: 110. Ambulance/fire: 119. ⚠ Don't plan on English on either line here: 119 is answered by the local fire headquarters, so any interpreter service is a municipal one that differs between Matsue and Oda, and nothing published for either confirms it. Work around that instead — where you can, have the lodging's front desk place the call; keep the ambulance and police phrase cards (Etiquette & language) reachable on a lock screen; and if you do call alone, give the place name first and repeat it slowly rather than hanging up.

Matsue has full-service pharmacies and hospitals near the station. Oda City has a smaller hospital and a handful of pharmacies in the town center; the Omori heritage district itself has none — anyone needing regular medication should carry it, not plan to refill it there.

The Iwami Ginzan mine trail and the Ginzan Cart route involve uneven ground, some stairs, and long stretches without shade or seating — pace the two low-mobility travelers' day around it rather than the group average (see Days).
